title: What You Know Now
description:
Sangchul poured tea.

Same as any other day. Charts, market, next month's strategy.

{name} took the cup and thought:
This man — he's the one who introduced the scammer to Dad.

Sitting here knowing that.

choices.text: Learn everything this person can teach — then decide
choices.result_text:
Took notes. Watched the charts.

A man's knowledge and his crime can be separated. At least for now. At least while it's useful.

Apologized to Dad in some private part of the mind. Kept going.

choices.text: This situation feels wrong and it won't let go
choices.result_text:
Hand paused mid-cup.

Sitting with the man who brought the ruin into his father's life. Calling it a lesson.
Whether this is survival or compromise — left early today.

title: What Was Left Unsaid
description:
'Forget it.'

Said that and took it back. Sangchul didn't bring it up again.
Neither did {name}.

An agreement without words. Something buried.

choices.text: This relationship still has value — keep going
choices.result_text:
What he knows is still needed.
When the goal outweighs the truth, this choice is possible.

Whether it was right — Gangnam will answer that. Or won't.

choices.text: Carrying this is heavier than expected
choices.result_text:
It should feel lighter — buried.
Instead it's the opposite.

That unfinished moment at the café table — 'how did you find out?' left unanswered — is still alive.
How to close it remains unknown.

title: He Called Your Name
description:
He called out as {name} left the café.
Didn't turn around.

That voice still carries.

Worked without him since then.
Without a mentor. Without a network.

choices.text: That was the right call — still believe it
choices.result_text:
Harder without a guide. But more earned.

What Sangchul taught is still in the toolkit. Even without him.
Learning where the line was — that's what standing alone requires.

His knowledge was useful. His network still comes to mind.

But not turning around was right.
The voice calling from behind — that's why the door didn't open again.

title: One Hour Before
description:
'One hour before.'

That sentence shows up in dreams.

The empty hospital bed. Don't remember if it was still warm.

Today, mid-work — the train window came back. Rice fields passing in the dark.

choices.result_text:
Late. But went.

What that choice means exactly — unclear.
But not going would have been worse. That's clear.

Wanted to prove something to Dad. That reason is still alive.

choices.text: Still think about that one hour
choices.result_text:
One earlier train.

That thought hasn't fully left.

But went. Arrived. Sat by the empty bed.
That's what was possible. That was all.

title: The Number and the Date
description:
The account number grew.

Since that day, every time it goes up, there's a pause.

'The number had gone up.'

That was everything, that day.

choices.text: This money has to pay something back
choices.result_text:
Can't be paid back. Not with money.

But watching these numbers grow — the belief that doing better is the repayment is what keeps this moving forward.

Wanted to prove something to Dad. That reason has to stay alive.

choices.text: This money doesn't fix what it didn't fix
choices.result_text:
Knew it from the start.

Made 5 million won that day. Understood the weight of the choice.

What that money is worth — still no answer.

title: The Calendar
description:
The calendar was full of circles.

Still on the wall. Couldn't take it down.

A gambling ad appeared on screen today. Scrolled past it.
The hand wasn't the same hand it used to be.

choices.result_text:
Someone who beat an addiction isn't someone who never fell.
They're someone who climbed back up after seeing the bottom.

One circle. Then another. That's what built this.
Leaving it on the wall was right.

Quitting wasn't one decision. It was a choice made every time.

Made it today. Closed the ad.

Choices keep stacking. Like circles on a calendar.
